text:
maria.k: Quick sanity-check — onboarding HF reranker (sentence-transformers variant) into Redwood embeddings shows different pooling behavior vs local HF. Our NDCG dropped ~6% in the initial eval run. Anyone seen subtle CLS/truncation mismatches?

raj: Hmm, can you paste the conversion command you used? Did you use the fast tokenizer?

maria.k: Used our usual hf->redwood script: `python tools/hf_to_redwood.py --model sentence-transformers/distilbert-sim` (default args). Tokenizer was AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained with no extra flags.

oliver: Two common gotchas: 1) HF models that rely on [CLS] for pooling vs sentence-transformers that mean-pool; 2) tokenizers with `add_special_tokens` / `cls_token` mapped differently in config.json.

sophie: Also check `model_max_length` and `truncation_side`. HF fast tokenizers sometimes set `model_max_length` to a huge value and rely on truncation at call-time; our conversion might be writing a smaller `max_seq_len` into the Redwood model config. That will change which tokens end up in the pooling window.

maria.k: Good call — printed tokenizer config on both sides:
```
# HF tokenizer.json snippet
{
  "model_max_length": 512,
  "padding_side": "right",
  "truncation_side": "right",
  "cls_token": "[CLS]"
}

# Redwood converted config (from deployed artifact)
{
  "max_seq_len": 256,
  "padding_side": "left",
  "special_tokens": {"bos": "<s>", "cls": null}
}
```

raj: There it is — max_seq_len mismatch and padding_side flipped. If the redwood config lost the CLS mapping (null) then any CLS-dependent pooling will now mean-pool or use first-token fallback, which changes embedding vectors.

oliver: Also the `padding_side` flip means token positions for attention + positional embeddings differ for short inputs if your pooling index is position-based. Rerankers are super sensitive to that.

maria.k: Re-ran a tiny comparison: token ids and lengths for the same sentence:
```
# HF (local) tokens -> [101, 2023, 2003, 1037, 2178, 102]  (len 6, [CLS]=101, [SEP]=102)
# Redwood converted -> [0, 0, 101, 2023, 2003, 1037, 2178, 102] (len 8, left-padded, CLS missing)
```

sophie: That padding shift + missing CLS explains the vector shift. Fix options: a) ensure conversion maps `cls_token` and `sep_token` to the converted special tokens; b) preserve `padding_side` and `model_max_length`; c) switch pooling to mean pooling or to explicit `pool_on_token: cls` after verifying CLS presence.

maria.k: If we switch pooling to mean, eval NDCG improves by ~2% but still below HF baseline. So it's not just pooling type; truncation is biting for longer queries (we had a 20% longer average tokens for dev set).

raj: Might be quantization compounding errors too. If you quantized weights (int8) and also changed tokenization, embedding drift stacks. What quantization config did you use?

maria.k: We tried fp16 -> int8 dynamic with `bits=8, per_channel=True` on the runner. The biggest delta was before quantization though (6% drop), quantized run added another ~1.3% drop.

oliver: Suggestion: create a micro-test fixture that compares normalized embedding cosine between HF and Redwood for the exact tokenization pipeline. Steps: 1) dump token ids and attention masks from HF `tokenizer.encode_plus(..., return_tensors='pt', add_special_tokens=True)`, 2) call Redwood's tokenizer endpoint or conversion output and assert equality, 3) if mismatch, patch conversion to copy `tokenizer.json` keys verbatim.

raj: Another subtle point: `use_fast=True` tokenizers (Rust) sometimes canonicalize spaces differently (`add_prefix_space`), impacting token boundaries. For sentence-transformers, `add_prefix_space` can change the token alignment. Ensure fast/slow parity.

maria.k: I found we were using `use_fast=False` in HF tests but conversion defaulted to `use_fast=True`. Great catch.

ci-bot: Deploy job #4582 started for model bundle redwood/sim-2026-03. Logs: config merge detected changes in `special_tokens` and `padding_side`.

sophie: For patch plan: 1) update hf_to_redwood to copy `model_max_length`, `padding_side`, `truncation_side`, `cls_token`/`sep_token`/`bos_token` if present; 2) add an explicit `pooling_strategy` key in the redwood model manifest (`cls`/`mean`/`first_non_pad`); 3) add CI micro-tests that fail conversion if token ids differ for canonical sentences.

maria.k: I'll push a PR with the conversion fixes and a small eval harness (10 queries) to compare cosine distance and NDCG. Will tag you folks.

raj: One more thing — document in onboarding checklist: "Verify tokenizer parity (token ids, padding orientation, special tokens) before rolling reranker into production." Saves hours. :+1:

oliver: Agreed. Also add a note about long input truncation policy: prefer `truncate_left` for queries where the tail is more important, but make it explicit per-corpus.

maria.k: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood-infra/hf-conversions/pull/72 (draft). Tests failing because of a stray `null` cls mapping — fixing now.

sophie: Awesome. If you want, I can run the 10-query eval on Dedicated so quantization parity is identical to prod.

maria.k: Yes please, thanks!
